content:
Overview

IBPS Bank Recruitment refers to the common recruitment examinations conducted by the Institute of Banking Personnel Selection (IBPS) for public sector banks in India. Through its Common Written Examinations, IBPS selects candidates for posts such as Probationary Officer (PO), Clerical Cadre (Clerk), Specialist Officer (SO), and Regional Rural Bank (RRB) officer and office assistant posts. It is one of the largest recruitment drives in the country, held every year through a transparent online selection process.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Age limit: 20 to 30 years for Probationary Officer posts and 20 to 28 years for Clerk posts (relaxation for reserved categories as per rules)
  • Educational qualification: Graduation in any discipline from a recognised university
  • For Specialist Officer posts, a professional degree such as B.Tech, MBA, or CA is required depending on the post
  • Candidates must be proficient in the official language of the state they apply for

Benefits

  • Stable government bank job with attractive salary and allowances
  • Career growth through promotions, transfers, and internal examinations
  • Additional perks such as medical benefits, leave travel concession, and pensionary benefits
  • Job security and social prestige associated with public sector banking

How to Apply

  1. Visit the official IBPS website during the registration window
  2. Fill the online application form with personal, educational, and category details
  3. Upload scanned photograph, signature, and required documents
  4. Pay the application fee online and submit the form
  5. Download the admit card and appear for the preliminary and main examinations as scheduled

Required Documents

  • Scanned passport-size photograph and signature
  • Educational qualification certificates
  • Category certificate, if applicable
  • Valid photo ID proof such as Aadhaar or PAN card
meta_title: IBPS Bank Recruitment: Eligibility, Exam Pattern, Apply Online
meta_description: IBPS conducts recruitment exams for PO, Clerk, SO, and RRB posts in public sector banks. Know eligibility, age limit, exam pattern, and how to apply online.

content:
Overview

Railway Recruitment Board (RRB) Exams are conducted by the Railway Recruitment Boards across India to fill various posts in the Indian Railways. RRBs recruit candidates for Group C and Group D categories, including assistant loco pilot, technician, station master, ticket examiner, goods guard, and track maintainer posts. With over a lakh vacancies announced in each major recruitment cycle, these examinations are among the most competitive government job exams in the country.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Age limit varies by post, generally 18 to 36 years, with upper age relaxation for reserved categories
  • Educational qualification ranges from Class 10 pass to ITI, diploma, or graduation depending on the post
  • For technical posts such as ALP and technician, an ITI or engineering diploma is required
  • Candidates must be medically fit as per the standards prescribed for the post

Benefits

  • Permanent government job with the world's largest rail network
  • Railway passes and travel concessions for self and family members
  • Regular pay, dearness allowance, and retirement benefits under the railway pension scheme
  • Healthcare facilities through railway hospitals and dispensaries

How to Apply

  1. Visit the official RRB website of the region you wish to apply for
  2. Register with a valid mobile number and email ID
  3. Complete the online application form and upload required documents
  4. Pay the application fee online, where applicable
  5. Track the exam schedule and download the admit card from the same portal

Required Documents

  • Class 10 and higher educational certificates
  • ITI or diploma certificate for technical posts
  • Scanned photograph and signature
  • Category and disability certificates, if applicable
meta_title: RRB Exams: Railway Recruitment Posts, Eligibility, Apply
meta_description: RRB conducts recruitment exams for Indian Railways Group C and Group D posts. Check eligibility, age limit, post-wise qualification, and how to apply online.

content:
Overview

Ayushman Bharat Health and Wellness Centres (HWCs) are the first pillar of the Ayushman Bharat programme, India's flagship initiative for universal health coverage. Under this initiative, existing sub-centres and primary health centres are upgraded into HWCs to deliver comprehensive primary health care closer to people's homes. The focus is on preventive, promotive, and curative services for non-communicable diseases, maternal and child health, and basic diagnostic facilities at the community level.

Eligibility Criteria

  • All residents in the service area of a Health and Wellness Centre are eligible to avail services
  • Services are available free of cost at government-run HWCs
  • No income or category restrictions apply

Benefits

  • Free consultation with a mid-level health provider at the centre
  • Screening and management of common non-communicable diseases such as diabetes, hypertension, and oral, breast, and cervical cancers
  • Maternal and child health services including antenatal care and immunisation
  • Essential medicines and basic diagnostic tests at no cost
  • Tele-consultation with doctors and referral to higher facilities when needed

How to Apply

  1. Locate the nearest Health and Wellness Centre in your area
  2. Visit the centre and register as a patient at the OPD counter
  3. Undergo screening and consultation with the health care team
  4. Receive medicines, tests, or referral slips as advised

Required Documents

  • Aadhaar card or any government-issued identity proof
  • Previous medical records or prescriptions, if any
meta_title: Ayushman Bharat Health & Wellness Centres: Services, Benefits
meta_description: Ayushman Bharat Health and Wellness Centres provide free comprehensive primary healthcare near your home. Know the services, benefits, and how to access them.

content:
Overview

Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK) is a national health programme launched by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare in 2011. It guarantees free entitlements to pregnant women and sick newborns in government health institutions across India. The scheme ensures that no woman or newborn dies due to financial barriers in accessing delivery care and treatment for neonatal illness.

Eligibility Criteria

  • All pregnant women delivering in government health institutions
  • All sick newborns up to 30 days of age treated in government health facilities
  • No income or category restrictions; the scheme is universal for institutional deliveries

Benefits

  • Free delivery, including caesarean section, in government health institutions
  • Free drugs, consumables, diagnostics, and blood transfusion during the stay
  • Free diet for the mother for up to three days after normal delivery and seven days after caesarean delivery
  • Free transport from home to institution, between institutions, and back home
  • Free treatment for sick newborns, including free drugs and diagnostics

How to Apply

  1. Register your pregnancy at the nearest government health facility or with your ASHA worker
  2. Avail the free entitlements directly at the facility during delivery and postnatal stay
  3. For sick newborns, approach the nearest government facility's newborn care unit

Required Documents

  • Pregnancy registration card or Mother and Child Protection Card
  • Aadhaar card of the mother or family
  • Referral slip, if referred from another facility
meta_title: Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram: Free Delivery Benefits
meta_description: JSSK provides free delivery, drugs, diagnostics, diet, and transport for pregnant women and sick newborns in government hospitals. Check benefits and eligibility.

content:
Overview

Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP) is a campaign launched by the Department of Pharmaceuticals to provide quality generic medicines at affordable prices. Under the scheme, Jan Aushadhi Kendras are set up across the country, including in district hospitals and medical colleges, to sell generic medicines that are substantially cheaper than branded alternatives. The scheme aims to make healthcare affordable for every Indian citizen.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Open to all citizens of India; there is no income limit or registration requirement
  • Anyone can purchase medicines from a Jan Aushadhi Kendra with a valid prescription
  • Individuals and organisations can apply to open a new Jan Aushadhi Kendra as franchisees

Benefits

  • Generic medicines available at 50 to 90 percent lower prices compared to branded medicines
  • Over 1,900 medicines and more than 300 surgical items and consumables in the product list
  • Quality assured medicines manufactured by WHO-GMP certified units and tested by accredited laboratories
  • Monthly free health check-up camps and free medicines on World Jan Aushadhi Diwas

How to Apply

  1. Locate the nearest Jan Aushadhi Kendra using the store locator on the official portal
  2. Carry the prescription from a registered doctor to purchase medicines
  3. To open a new kendra, apply online through the Jan Aushadhi website with the required documents

Required Documents

  • Valid doctor's prescription for purchasing medicines
  • Aadhaar card or identity proof
  • For opening a kendra: educational certificates, premises details, and bank account details as per the application guidelines
meta_title: PM Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana: Generic Medicines at Low Cost
meta_description: PMBJP makes quality generic medicines available at 50-90% lower prices through Jan Aushadhi Kendras. Learn how to buy medicines or open a kendra.

content:
Overview

The National Digital Health Mission, now known as the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM), is a Government of India initiative to create a digital health ecosystem across the country. The mission assigns a unique health ID, called ABHA (Ayushman Bharat Health Account), to every citizen and enables the secure digital storage and sharing of health records. It aims to simplify access to healthcare services and make health data portable across hospitals and service providers.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Open to all citizens of India
  • Any individual can create an ABHA number free of cost
  • No income or category restrictions apply

Benefits

  • One unique ABHA health ID for lifelong use across all healthcare providers
  • Digital health records that can be accessed anytime through the ABHA app
  • Secure sharing of prescriptions, lab reports, and discharge summaries with doctors and hospitals
  • Reduced paperwork and faster, better-informed medical consultations

How to Apply

  1. Visit the official ABDM website or download the ABHA app
  2. Create your ABHA number using your Aadhaar or mobile number and photo ID
  3. Link your health records and start sharing them with healthcare providers as needed

Required Documents

  • Aadhaar card or any government-issued photo ID
  • Valid mobile number
meta_title: National Digital Health Mission (ABDM): ABHA Health ID Benefits
meta_description: ABDM, formerly National Digital Health Mission, gives every citizen a free ABHA health ID for digital health records. Learn how to create ABHA and its benefits.

content:
Overview

Mission Indradhanush is a national immunisation campaign launched by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare to accelerate coverage of routine vaccines among children and pregnant women. The mission focuses on districts and pockets with low immunisation coverage, targeting children up to two years of age and pregnant women who have missed vaccine doses. Since its launch in 2014, the mission has been conducted in multiple phases and expanded under Intensified Mission Indradhanush to reach the most vulnerable populations.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Children up to two years of age who have missed any dose of the routine immunisation schedule
  • Pregnant women who have missed tetanus and other scheduled vaccines
  • Priority to areas with low immunisation coverage and hard-to-reach communities

Benefits

  • Free vaccination against 12 vaccine-preventable diseases including measles, diphtheria, whooping cough, tetanus, polio, and hepatitis B
  • Protection of children and pregnant women from life-threatening infections
  • Immunisation sessions organised at convenient locations near communities
  • Full immunisation certificate issued after completion of the schedule

How to Apply

  1. Check the immunisation schedule with your local ASHA worker or ANM
  2. Visit the nearest session site, anganwadi centre, or health facility on the scheduled dates
  3. Carry the child's immunisation card to every session for dose tracking

Required Documents

  • Child's immunisation card
  • Mother and Child Protection Card
meta_title: Mission Indradhanush: Free Vaccination for Children & Women
meta_description: Mission Indradhanush provides free immunisation against 12 vaccine-preventable diseases for children under 2 and pregnant women. Check eligibility and schedule.

content:
Overview

Pradhan Mantri National Dialysis Programme is an initiative under the National Health Mission to provide free dialysis services to patients suffering from kidney failure. The programme was launched to reduce the financial burden of dialysis treatment, which is often required multiple times a week. Dialysis services are provided at district hospitals and medical colleges through a public private partnership model, making treatment accessible to patients in smaller towns and rural areas.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Patients with end-stage renal disease requiring regular dialysis
  • Services are provided free of cost at empanelled government health facilities
  • Patients referred by government hospitals are given priority; no income proof is generally required

Benefits

  • Free haemodialysis sessions at district and sub-district hospitals
  • Reduced travel burden as more dialysis centres are established in smaller towns
  • Quality dialysis machines and consumables through the PPP model with private operators
  • Continuity of care with regular follow-up and medication support

How to Apply

  1. Get a referral from a government hospital or district hospital doctor after diagnosis
  2. Register at the dialysis unit of the empanelled facility
  3. Attend the scheduled dialysis sessions as per the hospital's rota

Required Documents

  • Doctor's prescription and referral for dialysis
  • Recent medical reports and kidney function test results
  • Aadhaar card or any government-issued identity proof
meta_title: PM National Dialysis Programme: Free Dialysis at District Hospitals
meta_description: The PM National Dialysis Programme provides free dialysis for kidney failure patients at government hospitals. Know eligibility, how to apply, and benefits.

content:
Overview

The National AIDS Control Programme is a comprehensive programme of the Government of India, implemented by the National AIDS Control Organisation (NACO), for the prevention and control of HIV/AIDS in the country. Running since 1992, the programme focuses on awareness, prevention of new infections, testing and counselling services, and free antiretroviral therapy (ART) for people living with HIV. It operates through State AIDS Control Societies and a network of integrated counselling and testing centres (ICTC) across India.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Open to all individuals who wish to test for HIV or access related services
  • People living with HIV are eligible for free ART treatment at government ART centres
  • Pregnant women are offered routine HIV testing to prevent mother to child transmission

Benefits

  • Free and confidential HIV testing and counselling at ICTC centres
  • Free antiretroviral therapy and CD4 monitoring at ART centres
  • Prevention of parent to child transmission services for pregnant women
  • Awareness campaigns and targeted interventions for high-risk groups

How to Apply

  1. Visit the nearest Integrated Counselling and Testing Centre at a government hospital
  2. Undergo pre-test counselling and voluntary testing
  3. Collect the test result and receive post-test counselling
  4. If positive, register at the nearest ART centre for free treatment and regular follow-up

Required Documents

  • Aadhaar card or any government-issued identity proof
  • No referral is required for testing; ART registration follows standard procedure at the centre
meta_title: National AIDS Control Programme: Free HIV Testing & ART Treatment
meta_description: NACO's National AIDS Control Programme offers free HIV testing, counselling, and antiretroviral therapy at government centres. Know eligibility and how to access services.

content:
Overview

Rashtriya Bal Swasthya Karyakram (RBSK) is a national child health screening programme under the National Health Mission. Launched in 2013, it aims to screen children from birth to 18 years for the 4 Ds, namely birth defects, deficiencies, diseases, and developmental delays including disabilities. The programme provides early detection and free treatment support for children identified with health conditions, reducing the long-term impact of treatable illnesses.

Eligibility Criteria

  • All children from birth to 18 years of age
  • School children in government and government-aided schools
  • Out of school children in the age group 6 to 18 years through community screening
  • Children in anganwadi centres for early childhood screening

Benefits

  • Free health screening for common birth defects, deficiencies, and diseases
  • Early detection of developmental delays and disabilities
  • Referral and free treatment support at district early intervention centres and empanelled hospitals
  • Follow-up care and support for children with identified conditions

How to Apply

  1. Screening camps are organised in schools and anganwadi centres by mobile health teams
  2. Parents can also take children to the nearest government health facility for screening
  3. Children identified with conditions are referred for treatment and follow-up as per the programme

Required Documents

  • Child's birth certificate or school ID
  • Parent's identity proof
meta_title: Rashtriya Bal Swasthya Karyakram: Free Child Health Screening
meta_description: RBSK provides free health screening for birth defects, deficiencies, diseases, and developmental delays in children up to 18 years. Check how screening works.

content:
Overview

The National Programme for Prevention and Control of Cancer, Diabetes, Cardiovascular Diseases and Stroke (NPCDCS) addresses the growing burden of non-communicable diseases in India. Under this programme, the focus is on the screening, early diagnosis, and management of common cancers, particularly oral, breast, and cervical cancer, at primary and secondary levels of care. Screening camps are organised at health and wellness centres and district hospitals, with referral pathways for diagnosis and treatment.

Eligibility Criteria

  • All adults above 30 years of age are eligible for routine screening
  • Persons with risk factors such as tobacco use, family history, or lifestyle diseases are screened on priority
  • Women are screened for breast and cervical cancer at community level camps

Benefits

  • Free screening for oral, breast, and cervical cancers at government facilities
  • Early detection improves treatment outcomes and reduces treatment costs
  • Free diagnostic follow-up and referral to district hospitals and tertiary cancer centres
  • Community awareness about cancer risk factors and prevention

How to Apply

  1. Visit the nearest health and wellness centre or participate in community screening camps
  2. Undergo the screening examination by the health care team
  3. If the screening indicates risk, complete the diagnostic tests and treatment at the referred facility

Required Documents

  • Aadhaar card or any government-issued identity proof
  • Previous medical records, if any
meta_title: National Programme for Prevention of Cancer: Free Screening
meta_description: NPCDCS offers free screening for oral, breast, and cervical cancer at government health centres. Know who is eligible and how to get screened.

content:
Overview

The National Mental Health Programme (NMHP) is a flagship initiative of the Government of India to make mental health services accessible across the country. The programme supports the District Mental Health Programme (DMHP) in districts, providing counselling, outpatient and inpatient psychiatric care, and community awareness about mental health. It also supports the establishment of mental health facilities in medical colleges and strengthening of central institutions for psychiatric training and research.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Open to all individuals requiring mental health assessment or treatment
  • Services are provided at district hospitals, community health centres, and primary health centres under DMHP
  • No income or category restrictions apply

Benefits

  • Free counselling and outpatient psychiatric consultation at district mental health facilities
  • Low cost treatment and follow-up for common mental health conditions
  • Community awareness and early identification of mental health issues
  • Referral support for specialised care at regional and central institutes

How to Apply

  1. Visit the psychiatry or counselling section of your district hospital
  2. Register as a patient and undergo assessment by the mental health team
  3. Attend follow-up sessions and collect medicines as prescribed

Required Documents

  • Aadhaar card or any government-issued identity proof
  • Previous treatment records, if any
meta_title: National Mental Health Programme: Free Counselling & Treatment
meta_description: NMHP and the District Mental Health Programme provide counselling, psychiatric care, and awareness at government hospitals. Know eligibility and how to access.

content:
Overview

The National Oral Health Programme (NOHP) is an initiative of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare to improve oral health across India. The programme focuses on school oral health screening, awareness about oral hygiene, and strengthening dental care facilities at primary health centres and district hospitals. It aims to reduce the prevalence of dental caries, gum diseases, and oral cancers through prevention and early treatment.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Open to all citizens, with priority for school children in screening camps
  • Dental treatment at government facilities is available at subsidised rates
  • Special camps are organised in rural and underserved areas

Benefits

  • Free dental check-ups and screening camps in schools and communities
  • Early detection and treatment of dental caries, gum disease, and oral lesions
  • Referral for specialised dental care at district and tertiary hospitals
  • Awareness sessions on brushing, diet, and oral hygiene practices

How to Apply

  1. Visit the dental department of your nearest government hospital
  2. Register at the outpatient counter for a dental consultation
  3. Follow the treatment plan and attend scheduled follow-up visits

Required Documents

  • Aadhaar card or any government-issued identity proof
meta_title: National Oral Health Programme: Free Dental Check-up Camps
meta_description: The National Oral Health Programme provides school dental screening, awareness, and subsidised dental treatment at government facilities. Check how it works.

content:
Overview

The National Programme for Control of Blindness and Visual Impairment (NPCBVI) is a centrally sponsored programme working since 1976 to reduce the prevalence of blindness in India. The programme focuses on cataract surgery, the leading cause of avoidable blindness, along with eye care for refractive errors, glaucoma, diabetic retinopathy, and childhood blindness. It operates through district blind control societies, vision centres, and eye care units in government hospitals.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Open to all citizens requiring eye care services
  • Priority for cataract patients and persons with visual impairment in rural areas
  • Free eye check-up camps are organised in communities and schools

Benefits

  • Free eye screening camps and vision centre services in rural areas
  • Cataract surgeries performed at government hospitals at minimal or no cost
  • Free spectacles for school children identified with refractive errors
  • Referral and treatment support for glaucoma, diabetic retinopathy, and other eye diseases

How to Apply

  1. Attend a nearby eye screening camp or visit the eye department of a government hospital
  2. Undergo the eye examination and diagnosis
  3. Complete the treatment or surgery at the empanelled facility as advised

Required Documents

  • Aadhaar card or any government-issued identity proof
  • Previous eye prescriptions or reports, if any
meta_title: National Programme for Control of Blindness: Free Eye Care
meta_description: NPCBVI provides free eye screening, cataract surgeries, and spectacles for school children at government facilities. Know eligibility and how to access care.

content:
Overview

The Universal Immunisation Programme (UIP) is one of the largest public health programmes in the world, providing free vaccination against vaccine-preventable diseases to all children and pregnant women in India. Under UIP, vaccines are provided free of cost at government health facilities, anganwadi centres, and outreach session sites. The programme follows a national immunisation schedule covering diseases such as tuberculosis, polio, diphtheria, pertussis, tetanus, hepatitis B, measles, rubella, and Japanese encephalitis in endemic districts.

Eligibility Criteria

  • All children up to 16 months of age under the routine immunisation schedule
  • Booster doses for children up to 5 years as per the national schedule
  • Pregnant women for tetanus toxoid vaccination
  • No income or category restrictions

Benefits

  • Free vaccines as per the national immunisation schedule at government facilities
  • Protection against serious and life-threatening childhood diseases
  • Immunisation card to track doses and ensure complete vaccination
  • Outreach sessions in remote areas to ensure no child is left unvaccinated

How to Apply

  1. Contact your local ASHA worker or ANM for the immunisation schedule
  2. Visit the session site with the child on the scheduled dates
  3. Ensure the immunisation card is updated at every visit

Required Documents

  • Child's immunisation card
  • Mother and Child Protection Card
meta_title: Universal Immunisation Programme: Free Vaccines for Children
meta_description: UIP provides free vaccination against 12+ preventable diseases for children and pregnant women in India. Check the schedule, eligibility, and benefits.

content:
Overview

Rashtriya Kishor Swasthya Karyakram (RKSK) is a national programme for adolescent health launched in 2014 under the National Health Mission. The programme addresses the health needs of adolescents aged 10 to 19 years, covering nutrition, sexual and reproductive health, mental health, substance misuse, non-communicable diseases, and injuries. It uses peer educators, school health sessions, and weekly iron and folic acid supplementation to reach adolescents in schools and communities.

Eligibility Criteria

  • All adolescents aged 10 to 19 years in India
  • In-school and out-of-school adolescents are both covered
  • Services are available at government health facilities and school health sessions

Benefits

  • Weekly iron and folic acid supplementation to prevent anaemia
  • Health education sessions on nutrition, hygiene, and reproductive health
  • Peer educator network for counselling and information sharing
  • Referral and treatment support at adolescent friendly health clinics

How to Apply

  1. Participate in school health sessions or visit the adolescent friendly health clinic at a government facility
  2. Receive counselling and health services from trained staff
  3. Collect iron and folic acid supplements as per the schedule

Required Documents

  • No documents are generally required for school based services
  • For clinic visits, carry any government-issued identity proof
meta_title: Rashtriya Kishor Swasthya Karyakram: Adolescent Health Services
meta_description: RKSK promotes adolescent health through nutrition support, counselling, and clinic services for ages 10-19. Check eligibility and how to access services.

content:
Overview

The National Leprosy Eradication Programme (NLEP) is a centrally sponsored health scheme working to eliminate leprosy in India. The programme provides free diagnosis and multi-drug therapy (MDT) for leprosy patients at government health facilities, along with disability prevention and medical rehabilitation services. It also focuses on reducing stigma through awareness campaigns and community-based care in endemic districts.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Open to all persons suspected of having leprosy
  • Free treatment is available for all confirmed leprosy patients at government facilities
  • Household contacts of patients are screened as part of case detection drives

Benefits

  • Free diagnosis and complete multi-drug therapy for leprosy
  • Prevention of disability through early treatment and self-care training
  • Rehabilitation support, including assistive devices for persons with leprosy related disabilities
  • Community awareness to reduce stigma and encourage early reporting

How to Apply

  1. Visit the nearest government health facility if you notice skin patches, numbness, or other leprosy symptoms
  2. Undergo clinical examination and laboratory confirmation
  3. Start the free treatment course and complete the full duration as advised

Required Documents

  • Aadhaar card or any government-issued identity proof
  • Referral from another facility, if applicable
meta_title: National Leprosy Eradication Programme: Free Treatment
meta_description: NLEP provides free diagnosis, multi-drug therapy, and rehabilitation for leprosy patients at government facilities. Know the symptoms, eligibility, and treatment.

content:
Overview

The National Programme for Control of Blindness includes a dedicated component for the prevention of blindness in school children. Under this initiative, eye screening camps are organised in government and government-aided schools to detect refractive errors, amblyopia, squint, and other eye conditions in children. Children identified with refractive errors are provided free spectacles, and those requiring further care are referred to vision centres and eye hospitals.

Eligibility Criteria

  • All school children, primarily in government and government-aided schools
  • Children in the age group of 5 to 18 years are covered
  • Special coverage for children with visual difficulties reported by teachers or parents

Benefits

  • Free eye screening camps conducted in schools
  • Free spectacles for children identified with refractive errors
  • Early correction of vision problems improves learning and academic performance
  • Referral for squint, amblyopia, and other conditions requiring specialist care

How to Apply

  1. School eye screening camps are organised through the district blind control society
  2. Parents can also take children to the nearest government hospital eye department for screening
  3. Children with identified issues are followed up for treatment and spectacle delivery

Required Documents

  • School ID card
  • Parent's identity proof
meta_title: School Eye Screening Programme: Free Spectacles for Children
meta_description: The school eye screening programme detects refractive errors in children and provides free spectacles. Learn how screening camps work and eligibility.

content:
Overview

The National Programme for Health Care of the Elderly (NPHCE) is a centrally sponsored scheme launched in 2010 to provide accessible and affordable healthcare for senior citizens in India. The programme establishes geriatric departments and OPDs at district hospitals and regional geriatric centres at medical colleges, along with community level care for common geriatric conditions. It addresses the rising healthcare needs of the ageing population through dedicated services and trained geriatric care providers.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Open to all persons aged 60 years and above
  • Services are available at government hospitals with geriatric departments
  • No income or category restrictions apply

Benefits

  • Dedicated geriatric OPDs for consultation at district hospitals
  • Management of common geriatric conditions such as arthritis, diabetes, hypertension, and dementia
  • Rehabilitation and physiotherapy support at regional geriatric centres
  • Health education for elderly persons and caregivers on healthy ageing

How to Apply

  1. Visit the geriatric department or general OPD of a government hospital
  2. Register as a patient and undergo assessment by the treating team
  3. Attend follow-up visits and rehabilitation sessions as advised

Required Documents

  • Aadhaar card or any government-issued identity proof
  • Previous medical records, if any
meta_title: NPHCE: Healthcare for the Elderly at Government Hospitals
meta_description: NPHCE provides geriatric OPDs, treatment, and rehabilitation for senior citizens at government hospitals. Check eligibility and services offered.

content:
Overview

Pradhan Mantri Jan Aushadhi Kendra is the retail outlet of the Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP), where quality generic medicines and surgical items are sold at affordable prices. These kendras are operated by franchisees, including individuals, NGOs, charitable institutions, and government agencies, and are typically located near hospitals and in community areas. Each kendra follows a uniform branding and pricing policy to make medicines accessible to every citizen.

Eligibility Criteria

  • All citizens can purchase medicines from any Jan Aushadhi Kendra with a valid prescription
  • Individuals with a minimum educational qualification and premises can apply to open a kendra as franchisees
  • Preference is given to applicants from weaker sections and those setting up kendras in underserved areas

Benefits

  • Generic medicines available at 50 to 90 percent lower prices than branded equivalents
  • Wide product range including medicines, surgical items, and wellness products
  • Assured quality through WHO-GMP certified manufacturing and third-party testing
  • Opportunity for entrepreneurs to run a government recognised pharmacy business

How to Apply

  1. To buy medicines, visit the nearest Jan Aushadhi Kendra with a doctor's prescription
  2. To open a kendra, apply online on the Jan Aushadhi official website with the required documents
  3. Complete the selection process and training, then start operations with the standard kendra kit

Required Documents

  • Valid doctor's prescription for purchasing medicines
  • For opening a kendra: identity proof, educational certificates, and premises ownership or rental documents
meta_title: PM Jan Aushadhi Kendra: Generic Medicines, How to Open Kendra
meta_description: Jan Aushadhi Kendras sell quality generic medicines at 50-90% lower prices. Learn how to buy medicines or apply to open a kendra as a franchisee.
